triage.headline: These symptoms need a doctor's evaluation — please visit a clinic or PHC within the next day or two.
triage.explanation: You have Fabry disease, a chronic condition that can cause burning pain in the hands. Because the appropriate medicines and doses must be chosen by a qualified doctor, self‑medicating could be unsafe. There are no emergency signs such as fever, swelling, or sudden loss of function, so an urgent but not immediate visit is appropriate.

flags.reason: Neuropathic pain from Fabry disease requires professional assessment for proper pain control.
Chronic rare disease needs specialist input; medication choices must be tailored.

flags.symptom: No fever, swelling, or skin infection mentioned
flags.reason: Absence of red‑flag signs lowers urgency to a non‑emergency level.

home_care_tips: Avoid extreme cold or hot temperatures; keep your hands warm but not overheated.
Gentle hand massage or warm (not hot) compresses can help soothe burning sensations.
Stay well‑hydrated and maintain a balanced diet to support overall health.
Do not take any new pain medicines or change doses without talking to a doctor first.
Keep the skin of your hands moisturised to prevent cracking or secondary infection.
warning_signs: Sudden increase in pain, swelling, or redness of the hands.
Fever or chills accompanying the hand symptoms.
Numbness spreading rapidly or loss of strength in the hand or arm.
Development of a skin ulcer, pus, or foul smell indicating infection.
Any new shortness of breath, chest pain, or dizziness.
triage.disclaimer: I am an AI triage tool, not a medical professional. This advice does not replace a real medical evaluation. Please see a qualified doctor or visit your nearest health centre, especially if symptoms worsen or you develop any warning signs.
